rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reader hitting chunk 5 cold hasn't met this term anywhere in chunks 0-4, so a definite-article reference reads as assumed prior knowledge it doesn't have — the exact 'Never named / forward reference' harm rule 1 exists to stop. Quoted at expanded line 51: 'You bring the voice of experience: the soft item, the step that contradicts how this codebase actually works.' 'The soft item' is used with a definite article as if already established, but the term never appears anywhere earlier in this file (chunks 0-4 name none of it). The only gloss ('Stuck naming a soft item? Ask Claude which step it's least confident about') arrives two chunks later at chunk 6 (line 59) — a forward reference, the canonical failure shape rule 1 names ('before the three things get named' pointing at a LATER slide). 'Soft item' is established training vocabulary (used throughout push-back-on-the-plan.md, plan-mode-done-right.md, trainer-modules.md) but this lecture is itself the FIRST place in the student-facing arc it would need introducing — the exercise that defines it sits after this lecture, not before, so the arc-earned-vocabulary carve-out doesn't reach it.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: At first use (chunk 5, line 51) swap 'the soft item' for a self-contained phrase, e.g. 'the step you're not confident about' — or promote the chunk-6 gloss ('the step Claude is least confident about') up to this first mention so the term is self-defining on arrival.

rules_evaluated.evidence: No harm present: the file contains no positional pointers to another file ('the opening lecture said...'); the one forward pointer ('The exercise will show you either way', chunk 2) is a navigational reference to the module's own next beat, not a cross-file positional callback.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No harm present: no 'the X you did/saw/caught' backward-pointing constructions appear anywhere in the body, so there is nothing that could strand against a missing beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No harm present: chunk 2's 'ask plan mode directly' beat is a live, open-ended student action ('Watch what comes back') with no narrated outcome placed above a guess — there is no guess-then-reveal ordering to break.
No harm present: every chunk (1-7) carries multiple self-contained bullets or a full checklist plus kicker; none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent line.

No harm present: each header's claim is backed by its own chunk's content under a projection-distance read (e.g. 'Five things a good plan has' is followed by exactly five bulleted criteria; 'Plan review is a high-leverage gate' is backed by 'One correction can redirect every step that follows'). No header is contradicted by its own body.

No harm present, checked sub-item by sub-item: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' triple (the two-part 'isn't X. It's Y.' contrasts in chunks 1 and 4, and 'Not today, but soon' in chunk 1, are single-negation two-part contrasts, not the banned three-part shape); no anaphora/epistrophe triple in continuous prose (the three- and five-item lists in chunks 3-4 are checklist bullets, not rhetorical repetition); no self-grading superlative ('high-leverage gate' in chunk 7 is a substantiated technical claim about the technique, backed by the body's own argument, not unearned self-praise of the course/exercise); no number-with-retraction; no verb triplet with an empty leg. 'The wrongness tangles with everything built after it' and 'you will not notice' (chunk 7) carry an explicit maintainer attestation dated 2026-08-08 not to soften them, which covers their unusual register under the maintainer-attested-phrasing carve-out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No harm present: none of the banned dialect terms (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun) appear anywhere in the body; 'session' is controlled AE101 vocabulary already established in the widget line, not repo-internal jargon.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No harm present: chunks 3 and 4 bold exactly one handle per checklist-item bullet (explicitly permitted by the rule's own 'checklist item names' clause), and every other chunk (1, 2, 5, 6, 7) carries zero bold — consistent with the 2026-07-09 emphasis pass the maintainer block records.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No harm present: the file is pulled in via `plan-mode-done-right.md:38` ('[Lecture: When a plan is good](lectures/when-a-plan-is-good.md)'), which the renderer wraps in a `.phase--lecture` element per `site/layouts/slides.js`, so all chunks reach the composed deck, not just long-read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No harm present: no header in this file uses hand-numbered position or a 'Phase N:'/'N.' step-content pattern; all `##` headers are named, non-numbered category headers, so there is no ordinal to drift out of sync.
